```{r}
#Countour

basemayottedf <- st_as_sf(basemayotte, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), 
                         crs= "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0")

basemayottedf <- st_transform(basemayottedf, crs = st_crs(myt_contour))
basemayottedf <- bind_cols(basemayottedf, st_coordinates(st_centroid(basemayottedf$geometry)))
```

#Fitting the IDE Model
#In Lab 5.2 we ﬁtted the IDE model to the entire data set. Here, instead, we ﬁt the IDE model to the training data set created above. As before, since this computation takes a long time, we can load the results directly from cache.

```{r}
# La profoncdeur a été zappé ici (oublié ce code)
basemayotte_bis <- basemayotte %>% 
  mutate(Month_num = lubridate::month(Date) %>% as.double(), 
         Year_num = as.numeric(as.character(Year)),
         Year_month = ym(paste0(Year_num, "-", Month_num))) %>%
  group_by(Year_num, Month_num, Year_month, Longitude, Latitude) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Magnitude = mean(Magnitude), 
                   Depth = mean(Depth), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  na.omit()

dim(basemayotte_bis)
View(basemayotte_bis)
```

```{r}
# pred grid
get_coord_limits <- function(x, y){
  list(lon = c(min = min(x), max = max(x)),
       lat = c(min = min(y), max = max(y))
  )
}


coord_lim <- get_coord_limits(basemayotte$Longitude, basemayotte$Latitude)
pred_grid <- expand.grid(Longitude = seq(coord_lim$lon[1], coord_lim$lon[2], length = 150), 
                         Latitude = seq(coord_lim$lat[1], coord_lim$lat[2], length = 150),
                         Month_num = 1:12)

pred_grid2 <- expand.grid(Longitude = seq(coord_lim$lon[1], coord_lim$lon[2], length = 150), 
                         Latitude = seq(coord_lim$lat[1], coord_lim$lat[2], length = 150),
                         Year_month = as.numeric(unique(basemayotte$Year_month)))


pred_grid_sf <- st_as_sf(pred_grid, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), 
                         crs= "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0")

pred_grid_sf <- st_transform(pred_grid_sf, crs = st_crs(myt_contour))
pred_grid_sf <- bind_cols(pred_grid_sf, st_coordinates(st_centroid(pred_grid_sf$geometry)))
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# Suppose que ton jeu de données s'appelle basemayotte

seismes_plots <- ggplot(basemayotte) +
  # Carte de fond (contour de Mayotte)
  geom_sf(data = myt_contour_lonlat, fill = "black", color = "white", size = 0.4) +

  ylab("Latitude") +
```

## IDW model

```{r}
library(sf)
library(gstat)
library(dplyr)

# Transformer basemayotte en objet sf
myt_contour_lonlat <- st_transform(myt_contour, "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84") %>% 
  st_union()

basemayotte_sf <- basemayotte %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)  # WGS84
```


```{r}
# Créer une grille régulière
# Étendre la bbox (bounding box) du contour
bbox <- st_bbox(myt_contour_lonlat)
bbox["xmax"] <- 45.8  # élargir la longitude max à 48

# Créer une grille régulière basée sur cette bbox élargie
pred_grid <- st_make_grid(
  st_as_sfc(bbox),  # convertir bbox en polygone simple
  cellsize = 0.01,  # résolution de la grille
  what = "centers"
) %>% st_sf()

```


```{r}
magnitude_myt <- basemayotte_sf %>% 
  split(., .$Year) %>% 
  lapply(function(Year_sf){
    # IDW interpolation
    idw_res <- gstat::idw(formula = Magnitude ~ 1, 
                          locations = Year_sf,  # doit être un objet sf/sp
                          newdata = pred_grid, 
                          idp = 5)
    
    # Convertir le résultat en sf et ajouter coordonnées
    idw_sf <- st_as_sf(idw_res)
    idw_sf <- st_transform(idw_sf, crs = st_crs(myt_contour_lonlat))
     idw_sf <- bind_cols(idw_sf, st_coordinates(idw_sf))
# Les colonnes "X" et "Y" existent déjà après st_coordinates()
    return(idw_sf)
  })

magnitude_myt$`2018` %>% summary()
magnitude_myt %>% lapply(head)
```

#La décomposition 
```{r}
library(fable)
library(tsibbledata)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)
```

```{r}
#La decomposition additive
decomp1<-decompose(newdata10,type="add")
plot(decomp1,col="blue")
```
#Représentation de la saisonalité
```{r}
seasonality=decomp1$seasonal
plot(seasonality)
```
#Représentation de la tendance
```{r}
trends=decomp1$trend
plot(trends)
```

```{r}
#La décomposition multiplicative
decomp2<-decompose(newdata10,type="mul")
plot(decomp2, col="red")
```
```{r}
Tend.add<-decomp1$trend
Sais.add<-decomp1$seasonal
Tend.mult<-decomp2$trend
Sais.mult<-decomp2$seasonal
```

```{r}
ts.plot(cbind(Tend.add,Tend.add+Sais.add),lty=1:2)
ts.plot(cbind(Tend.mult,Tend.mult*Sais.mult),lty=1:2)
```

Nous allons voir la qualité de nos estimations en comparant les valeurs exactes, la prédiction additive et la multiplicative.

```{r}
ts.plot(cbind(newdata10,Tend.add+Sais.add,Tend.mult*Sais.mult)
,col=c("black","#009999","red"),lty=1:3)
```
On constate bien une bonne différence entre les prévisions et les fréquences exactes. Cela peut être dû par la présence d'autres phénomènes

Nous allons utiliser les méthodes de de Holt qui mettent en évidence l'horizon delà tendance (pente) de la série dans le temps  T et qui ajoute un coefficient saisonnier la dernière.

Nous allons utiliser la méthode de holt winters qui ajoute un coefficient saisonnier sur les données.

\section{La méthode de Holt}
## La méthode de Holt: Pas de saisonnalité mais avec tendance.
Holt a étendu le lissage exponentiel simple pour permettre la prévision des données avec une tendance (Tt). Cette méthode implique une équation de prévision et deux équations de lissage (une pour le niveau et une pour la tendance) :
Ces prévisions sont linéaires et sont données par:



```{r}
Holt.add=HoltWinters(newdata10,gamma=FALSE, optim.start = c(alpha = 0.3, beta = 0.5),seasonal="add")
```

Nous pouvons regarder les deux modéle de prédiction:

```{r}
plot(Holt.add$fitted, col="blue", main="")
#Holt decomposition
```

```{r}
Holt.add$fitted
```
\section{La méthode de Holt winters}
## La méthode de holt winters: Méthode Saisonnière.
Pour la méthode saisonnière(Holt-Winters), elle met en évidence quatre équations dont une équation de prévision et trois équations de lissage (une pour le niveau, un pour la tendance  
et un pour la composante saisonnière).
En plus, il existe deux variantes de cette méthode qui diffèrent par la nature de la composante saisonnière. La méthode additive est préférée lorsque les variations saisonnières sont à peu près constantes tout au long de la série, tandis que la méthode multiplicative est préférée lorsque les variations saisonnières changent proportionnellement au niveau de la série:
La prédiction est donnée par:

Dans notre cas, nous remarquons que les variations saisonnières changent au cours du temps. Donc à priori, nous préférons la multiplicative.

```{r}
Winter1<-HoltWinters(newdata10,seasonal="add",optim.start = c(alpha = 0.3, beta = 0.5, gamma=0.7))
```


```{r}
Winter2<-HoltWinters(newdata10,optim.start = c(alpha = 0.3, beta = 0.5, gamma=0.7), seasonal="mult")
```

```{r}
Winter1$fitted
```

```{r}
Winter2$fitted
```

La visualisation des prédiction:

```{r}
plot(Winter1)
```


```{r}
plot(Winter2,main="")
```

```{r}
plot(Winter1$fitted)
plot(Winter2$fitted)
```

#Prediction with Holt-Winters

To plot the predictions made by forecast.HoltWinters(), we can use the “plot.forecast()” function. You specify how many further time points you want to make forecasts for by using the “h” parameter in 

```{r}
hw_model <- HoltWinters(newdata10)
library(forecast)
forecast_hw <- forecast(hw_model, h = 90)  # h = 20 → prévision sur 90 jours

```

```{r}
autoplot(forecast_hw) +
  labs(
    title = "Forecast of the number of earthquakes (Holt-Winters model)",
    x = "Time",
    y = "Number of earthquakes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
library(tidyr)

daily_eq_complete <- daily_eq %>%
  complete(Date = seq(min(Date), max(Date), by = "day"), 
           fill = list(n_seismes = 0, mean_magnitude = NA))

newdata10 <- ts(
  daily_eq_complete$n_seismes,
  start = c(2018, as.numeric(format(min(daily_eq_complete$Date), "%j"))),
  frequency = 365
)

```

```{r}

forecast_hw <- forecast(hw_model, h = 90)

autoplot(forecast_hw) +

       x = "Time", y = "Number of earthquakes") +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#View(base_train)
# Chargement des librairies nécessaires
library(glmnet)
library(dplyr)

# Supposons que base_train est déjà défini et contient les variables suivantes :
# base_train$Magnitude (réponse)
# base_train[, 3:5] -> variables explicatives : Latitude, Longitude, Depth

# Conversion en matrice (glmnet requiert des matrices numériques sans NA)
x_train <- as.matrix(base_train[, 3:5])
y_train <- base_train$Magnitude

# Validation croisée pour choisir lambda optimal
choix_lambda <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, family = "gaussian", alpha = 0)  # alpha=0 => Ridge
lambda_opt <- choix_lambda$lambda.min
lambda_opt

# Ajustement du modèle final avec le lambda optimal
M3 <- glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 0, family = "gaussian", lambda = lambda_opt)

# Affichage des coefficients du modèle
coef(M3)
```

\section{Analyse de Moran}

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 1. Chargement des bibliothèques
# ============================================================
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(spatialreg)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# ============================================================
# 2. Lecture et préparation des données
# ============================================================
# Lecture des GeoPackages
library(sf)

# Conversion en objets sf à partir des coordonnées
base_train <- st_as_sf(base_train, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
base_test  <- st_as_sf(base_test,  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)

# Puis transformation dans le bon CRS pour Mayotte
base_train <- st_transform(base_train, 4471)
base_test  <- st_transform(base_test, 4471)

# Vérification
st_crs(base_train)
st_crs(base_test)
```




#Solution : corriger les doublons avant l’analyse

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# Identifier et supprimer les doublons géographiques
coords <- st_coordinates(base_train)
base_train <- base_train %>%
  mutate(X = coords[,1], Y = coords[,2])
base_train_unique <- base_train %>%
  distinct(X, Y, .keep_all = TRUE)
# Vérifier combien de doublons ont été retirés
cat("Nombre d'observations initial :", nrow(base_train), "\n")
cat("Nombre d'observations uniques  :", nrow(base_train_unique), "\n")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# Identifier et supprimer les doublons géographiques
coords <- st_coordinates(base_test)
base_test <- base_test %>%
  mutate(X = coords[,1], Y = coords[,2])
base_test_unique <- base_test %>%
  distinct(X, Y, .keep_all = TRUE)
# Vérifier combien de doublons ont été retirés
cat("Nombre d'observations initial :", nrow(base_test), "\n")
cat("Nombre d'observations uniques  :", nrow(base_test_unique), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 3. Préparation des coordonnées et voisinages
# ============================================================
coords <- st_coordinates(base_train_unique)
var_spatiale <- base_train_unique$Magnitude   # variable à étudier
```

```{r}
# Refaire les calculs des voisins sans doublons
knn1 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 1))
knn2 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 2))
knn3 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 3))
knn4 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 4))

lw1 <- nb2listw(knn1, zero.policy = TRUE)
lw2 <- nb2listw(knn2, zero.policy = TRUE)
lw3 <- nb2listw(knn3, zero.policy = TRUE)
lw4 <- nb2listw(knn4, zero.policy = TRUE)

```



```{r}
# ============================================================
# 4. Tests globaux de Moran (pour k = 1 à 4)
# ============================================================
IM1 <- moran.test(var_spatiale, lw1, zero.policy = TRUE)
IM2 <- moran.test(var_spatiale, lw2, zero.policy = TRUE)
IM3 <- moran.test(var_spatiale, lw3, zero.policy = TRUE)
IM4 <- moran.test(var_spatiale, lw4, zero.policy = TRUE)

Resultat_moran <- data.frame(
  Voisinage = c("1er", "2e", "3e", "4e"),
  I_Moran = c(IM1$estimate[1], IM2$estimate[1], IM3$estimate[1], IM4$estimate[1]),
  P_value = c(IM1$p.value, IM2$p.value, IM3$p.value, IM4$p.value)
)
print(Resultat_moran)

# Interprétation automatique
if (any(Resultat_moran$P_value < 0.05)) {
  cat("\n✅ Autocorrélation spatiale significative détectée (p < 0.05)\n")
} else {
  cat("\n❌ Pas d'autocorrélation spatiale significative\n")
}
```


```{r}
# ============================================================
# 5. Visualisation des diagrammes de Moran
# ============================================================

moran.plot(var_spatiale, lw1, labels=FALSE, main="k=1", col="blue", pch=20)
#moran.plot(var_spatiale, lw2, labels=FALSE, main="k=2", col="blue", pch=20)
#moran.plot(var_spatiale, lw3, labels=FALSE, main="k=3", col="blue", pch=20)
#moran.plot(var_spatiale, lw4, labels=FALSE, main="k=4", col="blue", pch=20)
```

```{r}
W22 <- knearneigh(coords)
W22 <- knn2nb(W22)
diste <- unlist(nbdists(W22, coords))
up <- max(diste)

near5 <- dnearneigh(coords, 0, up)
lw_dist <- nb2listw(near5, zero.policy = TRUE)

```

```{r}
library(spdep)
# --- Test de Moran ---
# var_spatiale = ta variable d'intérêt (par ex. Magnitude)
Moran_test <- moran.test(var_spatiale, listw = lw_dist, 
                         alternative = "two.sided",
                         randomisation = FALSE,
                         zero.policy = TRUE)

# Affichage des résultats
print(Moran_test)

# --- Moran plot ---
moran.plot(var_spatiale, listw = lw_dist, labels = FALSE, 
           pch = 20, col = "blue", xlab = "Valeurs centrées", 
           ylab = "Valeurs pondérées par les voisins")

```

##Modelisation
```{r}
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(spatialreg)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Coordonnées de base_train
coords_train <- st_coordinates(base_train_unique)

# Construction du voisinage k=1 (tu peux changer k)
# Construction du voisinage k=1
knn_train <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords_train, k = 1))

# Liste de poids spatiaux
lw_train <- nb2listw(knn_train, style="W", zero.policy=TRUE)
```

```{r}
base_train_unique
lw_train
```

```{r}
# Modèle SAR sur la variable Magnitude
# Ici : Magnitude ~ Latitude + Longitude + Depth (exemple)
sar_model <- lagsarlm(Magnitude ~ X + Y + Depth + Year,
                      data = base_train_unique,
                      listw = lw_train,
                      zero.policy = TRUE)
```


```{r}
summary(sar_model)
```


```{r}
# Résidus
base_train_unique$residuals <- residuals(sar_model)

# Valeurs ajustées
base_train_unique$predicted <- fitted(sar_model)

# Carte des résidus
ggplot(base_train_unique) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = residuals), size = 2) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low="blue", mid="white", high="red", midpoint=0) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="Résidus du modèle SAR - base_train",
       color="Résidus")
```


```{r}
# Carte des prédictions
ggplot(base_train_unique) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = predicted), size = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="Prédictions du modèle SAR - base_train",
       color="Magnitude prédite")
# Coordonnées de test
coords_test <- st_coordinates(base_test_unique)
```


```{r}
# Matrice de voisinage pour le test
# On peut réutiliser le voisinage basé sur le train (proche voisins)
knn_test <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords_test, k=1))
lw_test <- nb2listw(knn_test, style="W", zero.policy=TRUE)

# Prédictions sur le test
base_test_unique$predicted <- predict(sar_model, newdata=base_test_unique, listw=lw_test)

# Visualisation des prédictions
ggplot(base_test_unique) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = predicted), size=2) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +

```

```{r}
# LISTE DES FONCTIONS UTILES A NOS ANALYSES

minuscule <- function(x){
  sapply(x, function(xx){
    xx <- tolower(xx)
    xx <- strsplit(xx, split = "")[[1]]
    xx[1] <- toupper(xx[1])
    xx <- paste0(xx, collapse = "")
    xx
  }) %>% as.character()
}

missing_cols <- function(x, trhld = 0.9) {
  idx <- which(colMeans(is.na(x)) >= trhld)
  x <- x[-idx]
  x
}


convert_hm <- function(x){
  y <- character()
  # which x is not a number
  y[grepl("[0-9]H[0-9]", x)] <- paste0(gsub("H", ":", x[grepl("[0-9]H[0-9]", x)]), ":00")
  a <- as.character(structure(as.integer(86400*as.numeric(x[!grepl("[0-9]H[0-9]", x)])), class="ITime"))
  y[!grepl("[0-9]H[0-9]", x)] <- a
  # y <- hms(y, roll = TRUE)
  y
}


# convert_hm(x)
count_zeros <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE){
  if (na.rm){
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  } 
  
  id1s <- c(0, which(x == 1), length(x) + 1)
  longest_run <- max(diff(id1s)) - 1
  
  longest_run
}


all_zeros <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE){
  if (na.rm){
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  } 
  sum(x == 0)
}

# a <- count_zeros(sample(0:1, size = 20, replace = TRUE))

# fonction qui compte le nombre max de jours sans pluies
comptage_0 <- count_zeros

nsp_max <- function(x, period = 7){
  n <- length(x)
  jumps <- seq(1, n, by = period)
  nval_y <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:(length(jumps)-1)){
    y <- x[(jumps[i]):(jumps[i+1]-1)]
    nval_y <- c(nval_y, comptage_0(y))
  }
  
  nval_y
}

# special function that will calculate the sum of and will return NA where all
# are NA and sum with na.rm = TRUE where there is non-NA value in list

sp_sum <- function(x){
  if (all(is.na(x))){
    return(NA)
  } else {
    sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

sp_mean <- function(x){
  if (all(is.na(x))){
    return(NA)
  } else {
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

sp_d <- function(x){
  if (all(is.na(x))){
    return(NA)
  } else {
    sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}


sp_func <- function(x, fun = mean){
  if (all(is.na(x))){
    return(NA)
  } else {
    fun(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}


# distance euclidienne
eucl_dist <- function(x, y) {
  sqrt(sum((x-y)^2))
}

r_dist <- function(x, y){
  d2 <- apply(x, 1, function(xx){
    apply(y, 1, function(y){
      eucl_dist(xx, y)
    })
  })
  d2
}

# cette function trouve les points les plus proches de x dans la base df a 
# partir de la distance
# @new_x: le nouveau point
# @df: la base de donnees contenant les n points
# @k: le nombre de proches voisins

knn_match <- function(new_x, df, x.name = "X", y.name = "Y", 
                      var_name = "commune", k = 1,
                      display_all = TRUE){
  n <- nrow(new_x)
  colnames(new_x) <- paste0("new_", names(new_x))
  df_xy <- df[, c(x.name, y.name)]
  
  if (n == 1){
    d <- apply(df_xy, 1, function(y){
      eucl_dist(new_x, y)
    })
    
    id_neighbors <- order(d)[1:k]
    df_newx <- bind_cols(new_x, df[id_neighbors,])
    df_newx
  } else {
    # for each new_x do what was done above
    for (i in 1:n){
      x <- new_x[i,]
    }
    df_newx <- apply(new_x, 1, function(x){
      d <- apply(df_xy, 1, function(y){
        eucl_dist(x, y)
      })
      id_neighbors <- order(d)[1:k]
      bind_cols("new_X" = x[1], "new_Y" = x[2], df[id_neighbors,])
    }) %>% bind_rows()
    
    if (display_all){
      df_newx
    } else {
      df_newx %>% split(., .$new_X) %>% 
        lapply(function(x){
          classes <- x[[var_name]]
          # find the modal class
          mod_class <- which.max(table(classes)) %>% names() %>% sample(., size = 1)
          x %>% filter_(paste0(var_name, " == " , "'", mod_class, "'")) %>% 
            .[1,]
        }) %>% bind_rows()
    }
  }
}


# use knn_match to add covariates to a grid
add_covariates <- function(grid, data){
  res <- knn_match(grid, data)
  res <- res %>% dplyr::select(-X, -Y, X = new_X, Y = new_Y)
  res
}

## 
nlastdays_cumul <- function(x, h = 7, FUN = sum, probs = NULL){
  n <- length(x)
  cumx <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:(n)){
    if ((i-h+1) < 0){
      if (identical(FUN, quantile)){
        cumx[i] <- FUN(x[i:1], probs = probs)
      } else {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(x[i:1])
      }
      
    } else {
      if (identical(FUN, quantile)){
        cumx[i] <- FUN(x[(i-h+1):i], probs = probs)
      } else {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(x[(i-h+1):i])
      }
    }
  }
  return(cumx)
}


consecdays_quantile <- function(x, h = 7, FUN = count_zeros, probs = NULL, direction = ">="){
  n <- length(x)
  cumx <- c()
  for (i in 1:(n)){
    if ((i-h+1) < 0){
      z <- quantile(x[i:1], probs = probs)
      if (direction == ">="){
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[i:1] >= z))
      } 
      
      if (direction == ">") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[i:1] > z))
      }
      
      if (direction == "<=") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[i:1] <= z))
      }
      
      if (direction == "<") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[i:1] < z))
      }
    } else {
      z <- quantile(x[(i-h+1):i], probs = probs)
      if (direction == ">="){
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[(i-h+1):i] >= z))
      } 
      
      if (direction == ">") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[(i-h+1):i] > z))
      }
      
      if (direction == "<=") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[(i-h+1):i] <= z))
      }
      
      if (direction == "<") {
        cumx[i] <- FUN(1 - (x[(i-h+1):i] < z))
      }
    }
  }
  return(cumx)
}


# kernel functions
Wt_IDW <- function(theta, dist_mat) 1/dist_mat^theta
Wt_IDW_gauss <- function(theta, dist_mat) exp(-dist_mat^2/theta)

# Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
LOOCV_score <- function(Wt_fun, theta, dist_mat, Z) { 
  Wtilde <- Wt_fun(theta = theta, dist_mat = dist_mat)
  CV <- 0
  # Zi <- c()
  for(i in 1:length(Z)) {
    Wtilde2 <- Wtilde[i,-i]
    W2 <- Wtilde2 / sum(Wtilde2) 
    z_pred <- W2 %*% Z[-i] 
    # Zi[i] <- z_pred
    CV[i] <- (z_pred - Z[i])^2
  }
  
  mean(CV, na.rm = TRUE)
}

best_tune <- function(theta_vect, FUN, df, x, y){
  # eliminate non-varying columns
  
  df_minmaxed <- df %>% ungroup() %>% filter_(paste0("!is.na(", y,")")) %>% 
    dplyr::select(all_of(x)) %>% 
    sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame()
  
  d <- rdist(df_minmaxed, df_minmaxed)
  
  a <- sapply(theta_vect, function(theta) {
    LOOCV_score(Wt_fun = FUN, 
                theta = theta, 
                dist_mat = d, 
                Z = df %>% filter_(paste0("!is.na(", y,")")) %>% .[[y]])
  })
  
  list(
    dist_mat = d,
    theta_vect = theta_vect,
    RMSE = sqrt(a),
    best_tune = theta_vect[which.min(a)]
  )
}


LOOCV_GAM <- function(f, df, Z, family = poisson(), method = "REML", trControl = NULL){
  CV <- lapply(1:length(Z), function(i){
    # cat("Iteration", i, "\n")
    m <- mgcv::gam(f, df[-i,], method = method, family = family, trControl = trControl)
    z_pred <- exp(predict(m, df)[i])
    (z_pred - Z[i])^2
  })
  mean(unlist(CV))
}

myt_contour_lonlat <- st_transform(myt_map_commune, "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84") %>% st_union()


get_grid <- function(m, length = 50){
  coords <- st_coordinates(st_geometry(m))
  coord_lim <- get_coord_limits(x = coords[, "X"], y = coords[, "Y"])
  
  myt_grid <- expand.grid(Longitude = seq(coord_lim$lon[1], coord_lim$lon[2], length = length), 
                          Latitude = seq(coord_lim$lat[1], coord_lim$lat[2], length = length))
  
  expanded_grid <- myt_grid
  myt_grid_sf <- st_as_sf(myt_grid, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4471")
  
  # myt_grid_sf <- st_transform(myt_grid_sf, "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")
  myt_grid_sf <- st_transform(myt_grid_sf, crs = st_crs(m))
  intersections <- st_intersects(myt_grid_sf$geometry, m)
  
  myt_grid_sf$commune <- m$commune[as.integer(intersections)]
  expanded_grid$commune <- m$commune[as.integer(intersections)]
  
  myt_grid_sf <- bind_cols(myt_grid_sf, st_coordinates(myt_grid_sf))
  
  list(grid_sf = myt_grid_sf,
       grid = expanded_grid %>% rename(X = "Longitude", Y = "Latitude"))
}


idw.predict <- function(df, x, y, FUN, theta = 5){
  Y <- df %>% ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(all_of(x)) %>% 
    sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame() %>% 
    mutate_(paste0("y = df[y]"))
  
  Y_train <- Y %>% filter_(paste0("!is.na(", y,")"))
  
  # distance
  d <- rdist(Y[x], Y_train[x])
  N <- nrow(d)
  
  # adjustment
  d <- (d*(N-1) + 1/20)/N
  
  # weight calculation
  Wtilde <- FUN(theta = theta, dist_mat = d)
  W <- Wtilde/rowSums(Wtilde)
  
  # predictions
  preds <- as.numeric(W %*% as.numeric(as.matrix(Y_train[,y])))
  preds
}


# climate_week_waste <- read_excel("./1. Egg_Resuls/CleanedData/climate_week_waste2.xlsx") %>% 
#   dplyr::select(-X, -Y)

get_predictions <- function(year, theta, df, map_grid, x, y, FUN, midpoint = NULL, climatedata, count_max = NULL){
  # climate_week_waste <- climate_week %>% 
  #   left_join(total_waste_week, by = c("NAME"="commune", "Year", "Week")) %>% 
  #   fill(waste_number, .direction = "down") %>% 
  #   filter(Year %in% year) %>% suppressWarnings()
  wks <- unique(df$Week)
  
  if ("X" %in% names(climatedata)) climatedata$X = NULL
  if ("Y" %in% names(climatedata)) climatedata$Y = NULL
  
  climatedata$Week <- week(climatedata$DATE)
  climatedata <- climatedata %>% filter(Year == year, Week %in% wks)
  
  myt_grid_sf0 <- map_grid$grid_sf %>% filter(!is.na(commune)) %>% 
    left_join(climatedata %>% filter(Year == year), by = c("commune" = "NAME")) %>% 
    dplyr::select(commune, all_of(x), X, Y) %>% suppressWarnings()
  
  expanded_grid0 <- map_grid$grid %>% filter(!is.na(commune)) %>% 
    left_join(climatedata %>% filter(Year == year), by = c("commune" = "NAME")) %>% 
    dplyr::select(commune, all_of(x), X, Y) %>% suppressWarnings()
  
  expanded_grid0 <- dplyr::select(expanded_grid0, all_of(x)) %>% sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame()
  pred_grid_idw <- dplyr::select(df, all_of(x)) %>% sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame()
  
  pred_obs_dist_mat <- rdist(expanded_grid0, pred_grid_idw)
  
  N <- nrow(pred_obs_dist_mat)
  pred_obs_dist_mat <- (pred_obs_dist_mat*(N-1) + 1/20)/N
  
  Wtilde <- FUN(theta = theta, dist_mat = pred_obs_dist_mat)
  rm(pred_obs_dist_mat)
  W <- Wtilde/rowSums(Wtilde)
  
  myt_grid_sf0$Pred <- as.numeric(W %*% df[[y]])
  expanded_grid0$commune <- myt_grid_sf0$commune
  expanded_grid0$Pred <- myt_grid_sf0$Pred
  expanded_grid0$X <- myt_grid_sf0$X
  expanded_grid0$Y <- myt_grid_sf0$Y
  expanded_grid0$Week <- myt_grid_sf0$Week
  # myt_grid_sf0$Ratio <- myt_grid_sf0$Pred/max(myt_grid_sf0$Pred)
  
  the_plot <- expanded_grid0 %>% 
    group_by(X, Y, Week) %>% 
    summarise(Avg_Num_eggs = mean(Pred), .groups = "drop") %>% ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(Ratio = Avg_Num_eggs/max(count_max))
    
  
  the_plot <- st_as_sf(the_plot, coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = "EPSG:4471")
  # the_plot <- st_transform(the_plot, "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")
  # 
  # the_plot <- st_as_sf(the_plot, coords = c("X", "Y"),
  #                           crs= "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0")
  
  the_plot <- st_transform(the_plot, crs = st_crs(myt_map_commune))
  the_plot <- bind_cols(the_plot, st_coordinates(the_plot))
  
  
  the_plot0 <- the_plot %>% 
    ggplot() + geom_tile(aes(X, Y, fill = Ratio)) +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "green", mid = "darkorange", high = "red", midpoint = 0.5) + #mean(the_plot$Ratio)
      geom_sf(data = myt_contour_lonlat, fill = "transparent", size = 0.1) +
      theme_map() + facet_wrap(~Week)

  the_plot0$labels$fill <- paste0(the_plot0$labels$fill, "\n", year)
  
  list(
    GridPred = myt_grid_sf0, 
    Plot = the_plot0
  )
}

# other version of the get_prediction function adapted for adult mosquito data
get_predictions2 <- function(year = 2018, theta = 5, FUN = Wt_IDW){
  myt_grid_sf0 <- myt_grid_sf %>%
    left_join(adult_mosquito_week %>% filter(Year == year) %>% dplyr::select(-X, -Y),
              by = "commune") 
  
  expanded_grid0 <- expanded_grid %>%
    left_join(adult_mosquito_week %>% filter(Year == year) %>% dplyr::select(-X, -Y),
              by = "commune") 
  
  myt_grid_sf0 <- bind_cols(myt_grid_sf0, st_coordinates(myt_grid_sf0))
  
  expanded_grid0 <- expanded_grid0 %>% rename(X = Longitude, Y = Latitude) %>% 
    dplyr::select(-Year, -d, -com, -commune, -Num_adult) %>% 
    sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame()
  
  pred_grid_idw <- adult_mosquito_week %>% filter(Year == year) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Year, -Num_adult, -d, -com, -commune) %>% 
    sapply(min_max) %>% data.frame() %>% 
    dplyr::select(names(expanded_grid0))
  
  pred_obs_dist_mat <- rdist(expanded_grid0, pred_grid_idw)
  
  N <- nrow(pred_obs_dist_mat)
  pred_obs_dist_mat <- (pred_obs_dist_mat*(N-1) + 1/20)/N
  
  Wt_IDW <- function(theta, dist_mat) 1/dist_mat^theta
  Wtilde <- FUN(theta = theta, dist_mat = pred_obs_dist_mat)
  
  Wtilde_rsums <- rowSums(Wtilde)
  W <- Wtilde/Wtilde_rsums
  
  myt_grid_sf0$Num_adult_pred <- as.numeric(W %*% adult_mosquito_week$Num_adult[adult_mosquito_week$Year==year])
  myt_grid_sf0$Ratio_adult=myt_grid_sf0$Num_adult_pred/max(myt_grid_sf0$Num_adult_pred)
  
  the_plot <- myt_grid_sf0 %>% ggplot() + geom_tile(aes(X, Y, fill = Ratio_adult)) + 
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "green", mid = "darkorange", high = "red", 
                         midpoint = max(myt_grid_sf0$Ratio_adult)/2) + 
    geom_sf(data = myt_contour_lonlat, fill = "transparent", size = 0.1) +
    theme_map() + facet_wrap(~Week)
  the_plot$labels$fill <- paste0("Predicted\nAdult ", year)
  
  list(
    GridPred = myt_grid_sf0,
    Plot = the_plot
  )
}

# function that does the Winsorization
correct_outliers <- function(x, method = "winsorization"){
  outliers <- boxplot(x, plot = FALSE)$out
  if (method == "winsorization"){
    x[x %in% outliers] <- sp_func(x[!x %in% outliers], fun = max)
  }
  x
}



# determine the growth (change in time)
growth <- function(x, percent = TRUE) {
  p <- ifelse(percent, 100, 1)
  p*(x - lag(x))/x
}


box_cox_transform <- function(x, lambda){
  if(lambda == 0){
    trans <- log(x)
  } else {
    trans <- (x^lambda-1)/lambda
  }
  trans
}


daterange <- function(start_date, end_date, by = "day"){
  date1 <- as.Date(start_date)
  date2 <- as.Date(end_date)
  y1 <- year(date1)
  y2 <- year(date2)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    Date = seq.Date(as.Date(paste0(y1, "-01-01")),
                    as.Date(paste0(y2, "-12-21")), by = "day")) %>% 
      mutate(Year = year(Date) %>% as.factor(),
             Week = week(Date)
  )
  df
}


# function that will add missing dates
get_daily_data <- function(observed_df, add = NULL){
  add %>% 
    lapply(function(commune){
      observed_df$commune <- commune
      observed_df
    }) %>% bind_rows()
}

get_ratio <- function(x, method = 1, threshold = NULL){
  n <- length(x)
  
  if (is.null(threshold)) threshold = max(x)
  
  if (n <= 1) {
      stop("x should be of length greater than 1!")
    } else {
    return(ifelse(x <= threshold, (x-min(x))/(threshold-min(x)), 1))
  }
}
```

```{r}
library(spatstat)
library(sf)
library(raster)

# Lire le shapefile de Mayotte
mayotte_sf <- st_read("myt_contour.shp")  # à adapter si le fichier est ailleurs

# Transformer en objet owin (window) pour spatstat
mayotte_owin <- as.owin(st_geometry(mayotte_sf))

# Liste des années
years <- 2018:2025

# Dégradé vert → rouge
colormap <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

# Nom du PDF
pdf("Seismic_density_Mayotte_2018_2025_contour.pdf", width=8, height=6)

for (yr in years) {
  
  # Filtrer les données pour l'année
  basemayotte_year <- subset(basemayotte, Year == yr)
  
  if (nrow(basemayotte_year) == 0) {
    warning(paste("Pas de données pour l'année", yr))
    next
  }
  
  # Créer l'objet ppp en limitant à la fenêtre (contour de Mayotte)
  myppp_year <- ppp(
    x = basemayotte_year$Longitude,
    y = basemayotte_year$Latitude,
    window = mayotte_owin,
    marks = basemayotte_year$Magnitude
  )
  
  # Estimer l'intensité inhomogène
  sigma_val <- 0.015  # Ajuster si nécessaire pour la résolution
  den_year <- density(myppp_year, sigma = sigma_val, at="pixels")
  
  # Tracer la densité limitée au contour
  plot(0, type="n", xlim=mayotte_owin$xrange, ylim=mayotte_owin$yrange,
       xlab="Longitude", ylab="Latitude",
       main=paste("Estimated inhomogeneous intensity - Mayotte", yr))
  
  # Ajouter la densité lissée
  plot(den_year, add=TRUE, col=colormap(128), main="")
  
  # Ajouter le contour de Mayotte
  plot(mayotte_owin, add=TRUE, border="black", lwd=2)
  
  # Légende
  legend("topright", legend=c("High density"), fill=c("red"), border=NA, bty="n")
}
```

```{r}
  # Ajouter légende (optionnel : seulement pour la première figure)
  if (yr == years[1]) {
    legend("topright", legend=c("High density"), fill=c("red"), border=NA, bty="n")
  }
}

dev.off()

```

```{r}
library(spatstat)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# Convertir le shapefile en owin
mayotte_owin <- as.owin(myt_contour)

# Liste des années
years <- 2018:2025

# Dégradé vert → rouge
colormap <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

# PDF de sortie
pdf("Seismic_density_Mayotte_2018_2025_contour.pdf", width=8, height=6)

for (yr in years) {
  
  # Filtrer les données pour l'année
  basemayotte_year <- basemayottedf %>% filter(Year == yr)
  
  if (nrow(basemayotte_year) == 0) next
  
  # Créer l'objet ppp avec coordonnées projetées
  myppp_year <- ppp(
    x = basemayotte_year$X,
    y = basemayotte_year$Y,
    window = mayotte_owin,
    marks = basemayotte_year$Magnitude
  )
  
  # Estimer la densité inhomogène
  sigma_val <- 0.015
  den_year <- density(myppp_year, sigma = sigma_val, at="pixels")
  
  # Tracer la densité
  plot(0, type="n", xlim=mayotte_owin$xrange, ylim=mayotte_owin$yrange,
       xlab="Longitude", ylab="Latitude",
       main=paste("Estimated inhomogeneous intensity - Mayotte", yr))
  
  plot(den_year, add=TRUE, col=colormap(128))
  
  # Ajouter le contour de Mayotte
  plot(mayotte_owin, add=TRUE, border="black", lwd=2)
  
  # Légende
  legend("topright", legend="High density", fill="red", border=NA, bty="n")
}

```
